title: The ISBA Bulletin
text:
Lindley Prize
The 2024 Lindley Prize was awarded during the banquet at the 2026 ISBA World Meeting in Nagoya. Congratulations to Jim Griffin, whose paper “Expressing and Visualizing Model Uncertainty in Bayesian Variable Selection Using Cartesian Credible Sets” won the prize, and to Changwoo Lee, Alessandro Zito, Huiyan Sang, and David Dunson, whose paper “Logistic-Beta Processes for Dependent Random Probabilities with Beta Marginals” received an honorable mention. I am also very grateful to all members of the Lindley Prize Committee for their careful and thoughtful work.
With one edition of the prize concluded, it is already time to look ahead to the next one. Papers presented at the 2026 ISBA World Meeting in Nagoya can be considered for the 2026 Lindley Prize, provided they are submitted to Bayesian Analysis by September 30, 2026. Authors should indicate in their cover letter that the paper is being submitted for consideration for the Lindley Prize and provide the identification number of the session in which the work was presented. Let me also add that those who have already submitted an eligible paper without indicating the prize can still enter by contacting me by the same deadline and providing the relevant session information.

title: The ISBA Bulletin
text:
Special Discussion Paper
It is a great pleasure to announce a special discussion paper in Bayesian Analysis: “Dependent Dirichlet Processes” by Steven N. MacEachern, his original 2000 manuscript. The paper is accompanied by “A Modern Perspective on Dependent Dirichlet Processes” by Steven N. MacEachern, Juhee Lee, and Hang J. Kim. Together, the two contributions combine the original formulation of what has become a highly influential class of Bayesian nonparametric models with a contemporary perspective on its development and impact.
We now welcome contributed discussions. Contributions may address the original DDP paper, the accompanying contemporary perspective, or more broadly the development, evolution, and future directions of dependent Dirichlet processes and related models. Discussions should be no more than two pages long and prepared using the BA style files, available through the Bayesian Analysis author resources on Project Euclid. Please submit your discussion via EJMS by October 15, 2026, selecting “Contributed Discussion” as the manuscript type and indicating that the discussion refers to MacEachern’s “Dependent Dirichlet Processes” (BA1610).

September Issue and Advance Publication
The September issue of Bayesian Analysis has just appeared, featuring 19 papers. Its somewhat larger size reflects our continuing effort to shorten the time between Advance Publication and appearance in a regular issue. I encourage you to explore these contributions, as well as the many excellent papers recently accepted and now available in the Advance Publication section.

BAYSM 2027: dates announced!
We are pleased to confirm that the next edition of the j-ISBA conference BAYSM will be held on April 12–16, 2027. The conference will take place entirely online, with an extremely low registration fee for j-ISBA members, ensuring accessibility for early career researchers from all over the world. Abstract submissions will open in October: stay tuned for news.

Organized sessions at conferences
We are organizing sessions at various conferences happening this fall, winter and spring:

International Day of Women in Statistics and Data Science (IDWSDS) 2026, held online on October 6, 2026. The speakers will be Federica Zoe Ricci (Swarthmore College), Louise Alamichel (Université Clermont Auvergne), Martina Contisciani (Goethe University Frankfurt), and Jie Jian (University of Chicago).
“New developments in Bayesian statistics: a j-ISBA sponsored session” at the International Indian Statistical Association (IISA) 2026, December 26-30, Varanasi. The speakers will be Vaidehi Dixit (University of Nottingham), Arka Banerjee (Indian Institute of Science Bangalore), and Miheer Dewaskar (University of New Mexico). Chair: Beniamino Hadj-Amar (University of South Carolina).
“Contributions from junior Bayesians: a j-ISBA session” at the LACSC-TIES-EnviBayes-EnvrASA 2026, December 7-11, in Mexico City. The speakers will be Carlos Carrillo-Gallegos (Columbia University), Marco Gallegos (University of Toronto), and Dafne Zorzetto (Georgia State University).

The session will feature three talks on flexible Bayesian methods for complex data, presented by j-ISBA members from different parts of the world: Santiago Marin (Australian National University), Maria Fernanda Pintado (CUNEF Madrid), and Ingrid Johana Guevara Romero (Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile).

title: The ISBA Bulletin
text:
Bayesian Deep Learning course materials
At the 2026 ISBA World Meeting in Nagoya, Julyan Arbel, Sara Wade, and Vincent Fortuin presented a short course on Bayesian Deep Learning, aimed at both Bayesians new to deep learning and machine learning researchers interested in Bayesian principles.
The course covers Bayesian neural networks, approximate inference, priors, symmetries and non-identifiability, marginal likelihood, singular learning theory, and scalable methods, together with a hands-on NumPyro practical comparing MAP, variational inference, and MCMC.
All course materials are available, including slides, YouTube videos, and practical materials.

title: The ISBA Bulletin
text:
Bayesian Deep Learning book

We are also pleased to announce the community-authored book Handbook of Bayesian Deep Learning. The pdf and Jupyter Book versions are freely available online.
The book provides a broad introduction to bringing Bayesian inference to modern deep learning. Its ten parts span Monte Carlo methods, Laplace approximations, variational inference, ensembles, kernel and Gaussian-process methods, neural-network priors, symmetries and non-identifiability, scalable inference, applications and software, and emerging research directions.
The book is intended both as an introduction to the field and as a reference for current research. Proceeds will support BayesAI activities, including travel support and prizes for researchers.

title: The ISBA Bulletin
text:
Join us in Edinburgh: BayesAI 2026
The inaugural meeting of the BayesAI Section will take place in Edinburgh on 26–30 October 2026, as part of the third workshop on Rethinking the Role of Bayesianism in the Age of Modern AI, following earlier meetings at Dagstuhl in 2024 and MBZUAI in 2025.
The workshop will ask what role Bayesian thinking should play in the next generation of AI. It will bring together researchers working across Bayesian statistics and machine learning to discuss uncertainty, reliability, robustness, scalable probabilistic reasoning, generative models, and other emerging directions. The programme will feature invited talks, discussions, lightning talks, and posters, with postgraduate students and early-career researchers especially encouraged to participate.
We hope BayesAI will provide an active home within ISBA for researchers working at the interface of Bayesian statistics and modern AI. Join the Section, and we hope to see you in Edinburgh in October!

title: The ISBA Bulletin
text:
Reports from events and conferences

European Seminar on Bayesian Econometrics (ESOBE) 2026 @Luiss, Roma
by the ESOBE Board




Participants at ESOBE 2026 during a session.


The 16th European Seminar on Bayesian Econometrics (ESOBE) was held at Luiss University in Rome, on 27-28 August (website). Over two days, the program combined keynote lectures by M. Conceptión Ausín (Carlos III, Madrid), Radu Craiu (Toronto) and Petros Dellaportas (UCL and Athens), oral contributed sessions, dedicated sessions for PhD candidates and early-career researchers, and two lunchtime poster sessions. Topics ranged from Bayesian computation and time-series modelling to forecasting, finance, causal inference and machine learning. The breadth of contributions and sustained engagement across formats confirmed the vitality of the ESOBE community.
The 50+ participants were diverse in origin and expertise, representing 14 countries across Europe, North America (Canada and the United States), and Asia (China and Japan), and including academic scholars as well as researchers from US and European central banks. More than half were PhD candidates or early-career researchers, whose participation was supported in part by travel grants from ISBA and its EFaB section. The dedicated sessions and poster slots gave early-career researchers substantial visibility and opportunities for direct exchange with established academics and practitioners. More broadly, the lunches and conference dinner at Villa Ada encouraged informal interaction among participants, helping to strengthen professional networks and the wider ESOBE community.
We would like to thank all participants for their contributions and for making the conference such an engaging event. The ESOBE Board warmly thanks Matteo Iacopini, Alessia Caponera, Marta Catalano and Marco Perone Pacifico for organizing a perfect event. We look forward to meeting again at the next ESOBE 2027 conference in Rotterdam.

Bayesian Nonparametric Networking Workshop 2026 @University of Seoul, Seoul
by Joungyoun Kim




Participants at the end of the 4th BNP Networking Workshop at the University of Seoul.


The 4th BNP Networking Workshop was held at the University of Seoul, Korea, from July 6 to 10, 2026, bringing together around 120 researchers and students from the Bayesian nonparametrics community. It was a wonderful week filled with interesting talks, lively discussions, and plenty of opportunities to meet old friends and make new ones. The workshop opened with a welcome reception and poster session, creating a relaxed and lively atmosphere for participants to exchange ideas from the very beginning. We were also very pleased to support the participation of early-career researchers, including students and postdoctoral researchers, through travel grants, helping them take part in the workshop and connect with the broader BNP community.
The week also offered several opportunities to experience Seoul beyond the conference room. During the mid-week excursion, participants visited Changdeokgung Palace, Jogyesa Temple, Insadong, and Namsan, enjoying a mix of Korean history, culture, and city views. The conference banquet was another highlight, featuring a traditional Korean samulnori performance that brought plenty of energy and excitement to the evening. We were delighted to host such a warm and engaged community at the University of Seoul and are very grateful to all the speakers, participants, organizers, volunteers, and sponsors who made the meeting possible. We hope everyone left Seoul with good memories, new ideas, and new connections—and we look forward to meeting again at the next BNP Networking Workshop!

Upcoming Meetings, Conferences, and Workshops

ISBA sponsored or endorsed events

Mini-symposium on Bayesian Structural Learning, 28-30 September 2026, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Karlsruhe, Germany.
The Bayesian Biostatistics Meeting (BAYES) 2026, 21-23 October 2026, Leiden, The Netherlands. This meeting is an annual gathering of biostatisticians interested in using Bayesian methods in life science and public health settings.
Rethinking the Role of Bayesianism in the Age of Modern AI Workshop, 26-30 October 2026, Edinburgh, UK. This workshop will serve as the inaugural meeting of the ISBA section on Bayesian AI. The gathering will bring together researchers exploring the frontiers of Bayesian machine learning and deep learning in a collaborative atmosphere.
International Conference on Statistics, Data Science, and Computing for the Environment and Climate Change (LACSC-TIES-EnviBayes-EnvrASA) 2026, 7-11 December 2026, Mexico City, Mexico.
Bayesian Methods for the Social Sciences 3, 9-11 December, University College Dublin, Ireland. This 3-day workshop will consist of one day of introductory tutorial sessions, followed by 2 days of talks and posters. The call for posters is open until October 16.
International Statistical Ecology Conference (ISEC 2027), 8-15 January 2027, Mérida, Yucatán, México. This is the main international gathering of statistical ecologists and an inclusive interdisciplinary conference at the interface between statistics and ecology. This event is composed of 2-day workshops (8-9 January) followed by the main conference (10-15 January).
VIII Latin America Congress on Bayesian Statistics and 18th Brazilian Meeting of Bayesian Statistics, 1-5 March 2027, Armação de Búzios, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
Bayesian Structural Learning (BAYST) Workshop, 1-3 March 2027, Karlsruhe, Germany. This workshop aims to bridge recent advances in Bayesian structural learning with applied sciences, fostering scientific discussion and collaboration between theoretical and applied researchers. Deadline for abstract submission: 30 September.
Bayesian Inference for Stochastic Processes 15, 31 May - 2 June 2027, Westport, County Mayo, Ireland.
Games and Decisions in Reliability and Risk 9, 3-4 June 2027, Westport, County Mayo, Ireland.
EnviBayes–INLA Workshop 2027, 21-24 June 2027, Glasgow, Scotland, United Kingdom.
International Conference on Bayesian Nonparametrics – BNP15 (2027), 28 June - 02 July 2027, Bergamo, Lombardia, Italy.



Other events

5th International Day of Women in Statistics and Data Science, 6 October 2026, online. The Caucus for Women in Statistics and Data Science (CWS), the Portuguese Statistical Society (SPE), and the American Statistical Association (ASA) organise this fully online conference since 2022 to celebrate the day for Women in Statistics and Data Science (11 October).
Frontiers in Statistical Machine Learning (FSML) 2026, 14 December 2026, Split, Croatia. This workshop aims to spotlight emerging and impactful topics in statistical machine learning that are rapidly evolving but have yet to receive significant attention in leading IMS and ASA publications. It hosts an open call for short paper submissions (deadline 19 October).
IMS International Conference on Statistics and Data Science (ICSDS) 2026, 15-18 December 2026, Split, Croatia.
International Indian Statistical Association (IISA) 2026 conference, 26-30 December 2026, Varanasi, India.
